lines: CURATOR: FEATURE TOWN — 14 LIVE ROOMS
Each doorway has a sign describing its room.
Every curator can repeat their demonstration.
CURATOR: Welcome to Pocket RPG Kit.
14 doors, 14 live features.

commands.prompt: What would you like to know?

lines: Read a sign, then walk through its doorway.
In each room, talk to the central curator.
DPAD walks. A confirms. B cancels.
L rewinds. SELECT opens demo controls.
Every demonstration is safe to repeat.
The return gate is beside each entrance.
CURATOR: 1. Screen Effects
A cottage garden for night tints, fades, weather, and camera moves.
CURATOR: 2. Map Animations
A waterside shrine where spell rings animate above and below the map.

events.name: Runtime Appearance and Layers information sign

lines: CURATOR: 3. Runtime Appearance and Layers
A costume workshop for live sprites, layers, and passage changes.
CURATOR: 4. Movement Controls & Routes
A terraced park where characters wander, run, route, and approach.
CURATOR: 5. Extensions & Live Choices
An oracle's salon whose choices come from live game-owned state.
CURATOR: 6. Battle Processing
A stone arena for a complete win, loss, or escape battle branch.
CURATOR: 7. Buy, Sell & Stock
A busy market with buying, selling, finite stock, and a shared wallet.
CURATOR: 8. Streamed World
A forest trail with streamed chunks, animated water, and tall walkers.
CURATOR: 9. Themes & Portraits
A portrait library where speakers and dialog themes change together.

events.name: Input Locks & World Idle information sign

lines: CURATOR: 10. Input Locks & World Idle
A small theater for locked-input scenes and world-idle gates.
CURATOR: 11. Saves & Save Codes
A post office that exports and verifies a real portable save code.
CURATOR: 12. Attract Tour & Rewind
A formal garden for the guided tour, takeover, and deterministic rewind.
CURATOR: 13. Sound Studio
A listening room for music, ambience, fanfares, cues, fades, and replay.
CURATOR: 14. Registration Desk
A staffed counter where the built-in name scene updates every greeting.
CURATOR: HALL 1 — Screen Effects
Commands: screenFade / screenTint / screenFlash
screenShake / camera / balloon / screenBackdrop
The curator in the center starts the demo.
First, the whole screen fades out and in.
One named tint moves day to dusk to night.
A zero-alpha target clears that named tint.
The camera visits a tile, an actor, and me.
Balloons work on every character target.
This persistent balloon waits for a clear.
The observer can carry one independently.
Backdrops persist beneath dialog.
An exposed backdrop is replaced by the next selection.
All presentation effects are clear again.
GUIDE: The lantern path still reads clearly after sunset.
VISITOR: Wait for the lightning over the reflecting pond.
I am a named camera and balloon target.
CURATOR: HALL 2 — Map Animations
Commands: mapAnim / stopAnim
The curator in the center starts the demo.
A waited one-shot plays above this tile.
Loops can sit below actors or follow them.
The ring followed; the pulse stayed pinned.
Stopping by id removed only the floor loop.
Stopping by animation removed both rings.
A bare stop removed every remaining effect.
A parallel stop released the waited loop.
GUIDE: The fountain and spell circles share the water court.
VISITOR: Some effects follow me; others stay on their tile.
My ring follows; my pulse stays behind.
CURATOR: HALL 3 — Runtime Appearance and Layers
Commands: appearance / layer / tileProperty
The curator in the center starts the demo.
Appearance targets the player, me, or an event.
The player appearance condition matched.
The named event condition matched too.
Null restored every authored appearance.
The screen layer starts with its day variant.
The same layer can switch to dusk...
...and night, with no map transfer.
Visibility is independent of the variant.
Map layers use the same command shape.
The tile override condition matched.
Empty edge lists explicitly open the tile.
Null restored the authored tile properties.
GUIDE: The mirrors make every costume change easy to compare.
VISITOR: Even this workshop gate can change while we watch.
The curator can restyle me at runtime.
CURATOR: HALL 4 — Movement Controls & Routes
Commands: moveControl / bounded wander / moveRoute
pathTo / approach
The curator in the center starts the demo.
Every actor was reset.
This demonstration is safe to repeat.
The gold curator now wanders inside
a four-by-three tile rectangle.
Speed plus run crossed the blocking crystal.
directionFix kept the runner facing up.
pathTo planned a route around live obstacles.
approach chose the anchor's left side.
The runner stopped nearby and faced it.
stop ended the repeating route.
moveType static also ended autonomous wander.
GUIDE: The terraces keep each walking route easy to follow.
VISITOR: Runners, wanderers, and followers all use the same map.
I demonstrate speed, running, collision,
and movement routes.
My random movement stays inside
the corner's four-by-three tile rectangle.
I block ordinary movement.
The through control can cross my tile.
approach picks a side, stops nearby,
and faces its target.
CURATOR: HALL 5 — Extensions & Live Choices
Commands: ext / extChoice
The curator in the center starts the demo.
CURATOR: This list belongs to game code.
Its labels and locks come from live reducer state.
CURATOR: Cancellation is data too.
The resolver recorded it without hidden state.
CURATOR: The Compass key was selected.
Stable keys survive a live list refresh.
CURATOR: The Lantern unlocks on a return visit.
Both ext state and variables updated atomically.
CURATOR: Gold made the Crown row available.
The provider read the live built-in wallet.
GUIDE: The oracle reads choices supplied by the game itself.
VISITOR: My favorite keepsake only appears when state allows it.
CURATOR: HALL 6 — Battle Processing
Commands: battle
The curator in the center starts the demo.
CURATOR: This arena is a pure battle reducer.
The map loop freezes while the scene owns input.
CURATOR: WIN branch resumed.
The arena wrote its result back to the session.
CURATOR: LOSE branch resumed.
Yielding is safe in this training hall.
CURATOR: ESCAPE branch resumed.
The parked event continued on its own branch.
CURATOR: The map loop resumed, then stopped.
Strike twice to win; Yield loses; Run escapes.
GUIDE: Every result returns safely to this training arena.
VISITOR: I am keeping score from behind the brass rail.
CURATOR: HALL 7 — Buy, Sell & Stock
Commands: shop
The curator in the center starts the demo.
CURATOR: Spend the shared 80 gold, then try selling.
Stock and inventory live in session state.
CURATOR: The same shop id keeps its remaining stock.
Open it again to see the persisted counters.
GUIDE: The clerk remembers stock after every purchase.
VISITOR: I compare prices before spending our shared gold.
CURATOR: HALL 8 — Streamed World
Commands: streamed chunks / animated tiles
16x32 walker
The curator in the center starts the demo.
CURATOR: This room is not a baked bitmap.
Its 128px chunks enter and leave a viewport pool.
CURATOR: Water sparks use native atlas animation.
Your two-tile-tall walker stays foot-anchored.
GUIDE: Only the nearby forest chunks stay resident.
VISITOR: The river keeps moving while the trail streams ahead.
CURATOR: HALL 9 — Themes & Portraits
Commands: GameView theme / speaker portrait
choices icon
The curator in the center starts the demo.
CURATOR: This is the gallery's midnight theme.
My name prefix selects a 64px portrait.
CURATOR: The same dialog now uses the sunrise theme.
Theme colors belong to the application, not saves.
GUIDE: A portrait gives every line a clear speaker.
VISITOR: I prefer the warm sunrise reading theme.

commands.prompt: Pick a partner to walk with you.

lines: CURATOR: Splendid. I know every shelf by heart.
GUIDE: Lead on. I will keep an eye on the map.
VISITOR: Oh, me? I would love the company!
The library is quiet. You browse on your own.
Take your time. The partners will wait here.
CURATOR: HALL 10 — Input Locks & World Idle
Commands: lockInput / unlockInput / worldIdle
The curator in the center starts the demo.
The next pause locks walking and new interactions.
The observers were reset for a fresh run.
Input is unlocked; this action is still active.
The worldIdle autorun waits for it to end.
GUIDE: The house lights mark when the stage owns input.
VISITOR: I wait for the scene to finish before taking my cue.
worldIdle is true: input is unlocked,
and the initiating action has ended.
The parallel observer saw the lock as busy.
The idle proof started too early.
Run the demonstration again to reset it.
CURATOR: HALL 11 — Saves & Save Codes
Commands: SaveMenu / encodeSaveCode / decodeSaveCode
The curator in the center starts the demo.
CURATOR: The app will snapshot this safe point.
Watch the real SaveMenu show export and import.
GUIDE: The counter handles export and import at one safe point.
VISITOR: A save code fits in a letter and survives the trip.
CURATOR: HALL 12 — Attract Tour & Rewind
Commands: attract tape / takeover / rewind
The curator in the center starts the demo.
CURATOR: Leave the controls idle for ten seconds.
The recorded tour visits every room at every rate.
Press any key to take over; press L to rewind.
SELECT opens chapters and map warp.
GUIDE: Leave the controls alone and the tour begins here.
VISITOR: Taking over and rewinding never changes the recorded route.
CURATOR: HALL 13 — Sound Studio
Commands: playBgm/Bgs/Me/Se / pause/resume
fade/replay
The curator in the center starts the demo.
CURATOR: Town music and crystal ambience mix live.
The coin chime is a one-shot sound effect.
CURATOR: The melody is paused now.
Confirm to resume, fade, and restore it.
CURATOR: The saved melody returns at its old position.
Music, ambience, fanfares, and cues share one clock.
GUIDE: Each listening booth isolates a different channel.
VISITOR: Music, ambience, fanfare, and cues can overlap cleanly.
CURATOR: HALL 14 — Registration Desk
Commands: scene / rpgkit.nameInput / {name}
The curator in the center starts the demo.
CURATOR: Welcome to the registration desk.
Enter a name and I will use it right away.
CURATOR: Welcome, {name}! Your badge is ready.
The player name now belongs to session and save state.
CURATOR: No problem, {name}.
The desk stays open whenever you are ready.
GUIDE: The registrar can update the name used by every dialog.
VISITOR: I signed in once; the staff remembered me everywhere.
